page_title: Things you forgot (or never knew) because of React

sources.entry: Things you forgot (or never knew) because of React

summary.title: Things you forgot (or never knew) because of React
summary.one_liner: React is an opinionated, aging framework, and many features it lacks or makes hard (web components, hooks ergonomics, server rendering, forms, styling, scaling) are handled more simply by newer frameworks and the web platform.
takeaways: Web components are missing from React for years and still lack a firm implementation commitment, while other frameworks already support them.
React hooks are now baseline; Preact Signals, Svelte stores, Solid Signals and Vue's composition API are presented as simpler or faster alternatives.
Other frameworks largely avoid manual render micromanagement (useMemo, useCallback, useEffect dependency arrays) and handle rendering by default.
Server-side rendering and two-way data binding for forms are default or simpler in SvelteKit, Vue, Astro and others than in React.
The author argues that ecosystem size and scalability worries are outdated, since vanilla JS packages and the platform often work across frameworks.
summary.summary: The author, Josh Collinsworth, uses a music-and-defaults analogy to argue that developers who only use React may not realize how far frontend has moved on. The post is an opinion piece with a list of areas where he says React lags: web components, hooks, rendering control, ecosystem and scaling concerns, server-side rendering, forms and two-way data binding, and styling. Each section compares React with frameworks such as Vue, Svelte, Preact, Solid, Astro and Fresh, and cites no benchmarks directly. The page is one-sided and its claims are the author's own judgement rather than measured results.
